_comment: Per-project placeholder substitutions applied by /sync-dev-kit. See handbook §9.7 for the full walkthrough. Most keys match {{KEY}} markers in kit templates (canonical model); some are runtime-read by kit scripts via `jq` directly (e.g. GEMINI_NOT_INSTALLED) — see §9.7 'Runtime-read placeholders'. Values are the real project-specific strings.

_placeholders_referenced_by_kit.GITFLOW_PROJECT_ID: GraphQL node ID of the GitHub Project (Projects v2) that issues for this repo are tracked in. Discover with: gh api graphql -f query='{ organization(login:"<ORG>") { projectsV2(first:10) { nodes { id title } } } }'. Empty value = gitflow project integration disabled (issue linking still works; the project board just doesn't auto-update). Used in gitflow-project.conf.
_placeholders_referenced_by_kit.GITFLOW_STATUS_FIELD_ID: GraphQL field ID of the Status single-select field on the project. Discover with: gh api graphql -f query='{ node(id:"<PROJECT_ID>") { ... on ProjectV2 { fields(first:20) { nodes { ... on ProjectV2SingleSelectField { id name options { id name } } } } } } }'. Empty value = gitflow project integration disabled. Used in gitflow-project.conf.
_placeholders_referenced_by_kit.GITFLOW_STATUS_IN_PROGRESS_ID: GraphQL option ID of the 'In Progress' value within the Status field (from same query as GITFLOW_STATUS_FIELD_ID). Set by /work <N>, which also assigns the issue to the gh user. Used in gitflow-project.conf. Required when GITFLOW_PROJECT_ID is set: empty fails /work <N> loud.
_placeholders_referenced_by_kit.GITFLOW_STATUS_STAGED_ID: GraphQL option ID of the 'Staged' value within the Status field — code complete, waiting for deployment. Set by /commit and /ship-main for each linked issue answered code complete, and by /open-pr for every linked issue (/open-pr refuses to open while any linked issue is unconfirmed). Discover with the same query as GITFLOW_STATUS_FIELD_ID — look for the 'Staged' option's `id` under the Status field's `options`. Used in gitflow-project.conf. Required when GITFLOW_PROJECT_ID is set: empty fails /commit, /ship-main and /open-pr loud.
_placeholders_referenced_by_kit.GITFLOW_STATUS_DEPLOYED_ID: GraphQL option ID of the Status value /deploy sets after the tag push, for every issue named by `Closes #N` since the last tag. The column may be called anything — Done, Deployed, Shipped. Gitflow never closes an issue itself: closing is the repository's 'Auto-close issues with merged linked pull requests' setting plus the board's 'Auto-close issue' workflow (project-documentation/github-project-board-setup.md). Discover with the same query as GITFLOW_STATUS_FIELD_ID — the chosen column's option `id`. Used in gitflow-project.conf. Required when GITFLOW_PROJECT_ID is set: empty fails /deploy loud.
_placeholders_referenced_by_kit.GEMINI_NOT_INSTALLED: Inverted-default toggle that records whether the Gemini Code Assist GitHub App is ABSENT from this repo. DEFAULT (missing/empty) = Gemini is installed → wait-for-pr-ready.sh blocks /open-pr, /triage, /merge until Gemini has reviewed current HEAD (15min fail-loud timeout). Set to 'true' ONLY when Gemini is genuinely not installed → gating skipped. The naming intentionally captures a FACT about the repo (presence of an external service), not a configuration preference, so the meaning of each state is unambiguous: empty = 'Gemini is installed' (the common case for this shop); 'true' = 'Gemini is not installed' (the exception for repos pending the App install). Detection: install via https://github.com/marketplace/gemini-code-assist for the org, OR run `gh api orgs/<org>/installations --jq '[.installations[] | select(.app_slug=="gemini-code-assist")] | length'` — non-zero count confirms installed. RUNTIME-READ placeholder: consumed by gitflow scripts directly via `jq -r '.GEMINI_NOT_INSTALLED // ""' .claude/sync-substitutions.json` at execution time, NOT substituted into any kit template at sync time. See handbook §9.7 'Runtime-read placeholders' note. SEMANTIC INVERSION FROM GITFLOW_* KEYS: GITFLOW_* keys treat empty as 'feature disabled' because those keys are required values; GEMINI_NOT_INSTALLED treats empty as 'feature enabled' because the name encodes a negation. Do not try to harmonize the two patterns.
_placeholders_referenced_by_kit.DEPLOY_WORKFLOWS: Space-separated list of deploy names, one per service, that /deploy dispatches after it pushes the release commit and tag. Single-app example: 'deploy.yml'. Split-deploy example: 'deploy-shop.yml deploy-dealer.yml'. Empty/missing → deploy.sh falls back to 'deploy.yml' (the kit default) UNLESS MIGRATE_WORKFLOW is set, in which case empty means a migration-only deploy with no app artifact (no deploy.yml fallback). Under DEPLOY_BACKEND=codebuild (the stance) these are names, not files: each maps to a CodeBuild project by CODEBUILD_PROJECT_PREFIX, and the fleet is dispatched concurrently and polled together. Under the github fallback each MUST be a real workflow with `workflow_dispatch:` as a trigger, living in this repo's .github/workflows/, triggered in turn and (unless --no-watch) watched sequentially via `gh run watch`. RUNTIME-READ placeholder: consumed by deploy.sh via `jq -r '.DEPLOY_WORKFLOWS // ""' .claude/sync-substitutions.json` at execution time, NOT substituted into any kit template at sync time. The --workflow CLI flag (repeatable) overrides the substitution for one-off invocations. See handbook §6.5.
_placeholders_referenced_by_kit.FORM_LIB_EXEMPT_APPS: Space-separated list of app names (the directory under apps/) that DELIBERATELY use no form library. Form-library adoption is decided PER APP and is all-in within an app: a mixed 'library here, hand-rolled there' rule produces one inconsistent decision per screen, which is the worst possible shape for an AI-written codebase. There are three states and the third is a hard build failure: (1) the app declares @tanstack/react-form -> decided yes, nothing recorded here; (2) the app is listed in this key -> deliberately decided no; (3) the app is in neither -> the question has NEVER BEEN ASKED, and scripts/check-stack.mjs fails until someone answers it. That third state is the whole point: dependency presence alone cannot distinguish 'we decided against it' from 'nobody has thought about it yet'. Exempt suits apps with no real data entry - ecommerce/cart surfaces, marketing pages, and control-plane or service apps whose UI is a couple of status screens. Data-entry apps (ERP browses and record forms) take the library. Scope: only apps/* workspaces that declare `react` are asked; headless apps (workers, REST services, shared) declare none and are correctly out of scope. RUNTIME-READ placeholder: consumed by scripts/check-stack.mjs directly via `jq -r '.FORM_LIB_EXEMPT_APPS // ""' .claude/sync-substitutions.json` at execution time, NOT substituted into any kit template at sync time. See handbook 9.7 'Runtime-read placeholders'. Empty/missing means no app is exempt, which is the correct default - it fails loudly for every front-end app until each one is deliberately answered.
_placeholders_referenced_by_kit.MIGRATE_WORKFLOW: Single migration name (a `migrate.yml`-shaped name) that /deploy runs as STEP 1 — once, BEFORE any app deploy in DEPLOY_WORKFLOWS, watched to completion and GATED (a real migration failure aborts the deploy before any app ships). Use for a DB-migration workflow (e.g. drizzle-kit migrate against the production DATABASE_URL). Empty/missing → no migration phase. Under DEPLOY_BACKEND=codebuild (the stance) the name maps to the migrate CodeBuild project by CODEBUILD_PROJECT_PREFIX, or CODEBUILD_MIGRATE_PROJECT when it does not follow that pattern; under the github fallback it is a workflow in .github/workflows/ whose ONLY trigger is `workflow_dispatch:`. Either way the migration MUST exit 0 on a no-op (no pending migrations) and non-zero only on a genuine failure — drizzle-kit can emit error-shaped output on a clean no-op, so the migration body (the migrate buildspec under codebuild) is responsible for trapping that. Migration is NEVER invoked on its own; it exists only as deploy's first phase (you would never migrate without deploying). A repo that maintains a database but ships no app (MIGRATE_WORKFLOW set + DEPLOY_WORKFLOWS empty) gets a migration-only deploy. RUNTIME-READ placeholder: consumed by deploy.sh via `jq -r '.MIGRATE_WORKFLOW // ""' .claude/sync-substitutions.json` at execution time, NOT substituted into any kit template at sync time. The --migrate-workflow CLI flag overrides the substitution for one-off invocations. See handbook §6.5.
_placeholders_referenced_by_kit.MIGRATE_PATHS: Space-separated git pathspec(s) of the directory/files that hold this project's migration files (e.g. 'apps/shared/src/db/migrations' for drizzle-kit; 'prisma/migrations' for Prisma; 'alembic/versions' for Alembic). Enables the /deploy migration-skip optimization: before firing MIGRATE_WORKFLOW, deploy.sh runs `git diff --name-only <last-tag>..HEAD -- <MIGRATE_PATHS>` and, if nothing under these paths changed since the last deploy, SKIPS the migration entirely — no build started (that ~2 min is build boot + npm ci just to reach a drizzle-kit no-op). The reference is the PREVIOUS deploy's tag (deploy.sh's LAST_TAG, captured before this run tags), so a migration that FAILED on a prior deploy is unaffected: that deploy's tag exists → re-running /deploy stops at the 'no commits since tag' gate → the operator's documented manual recovery applies it, and the migration stays idempotent as the backstop. Empty/missing → NO skip; MIGRATE_WORKFLOW always fires (prior behavior). Only meaningful when MIGRATE_WORKFLOW is set. RUNTIME-READ placeholder: consumed by deploy.sh via `jq -r '.MIGRATE_PATHS // ""' .claude/sync-substitutions.json` at execution time, NOT substituted into any kit template at sync time. The --migrate-paths CLI flag overrides the substitution for one-off invocations. See handbook §6.5.
_placeholders_referenced_by_kit.DEPLOY_BACKEND: Which release path /deploy dispatches to, and the ONLY question it answers is what else this project must have set. FOUR values, matched EXACTLY and case-sensitive. "codebuild" (the DEFAULT and the stance) starts AWS CodeBuild projects via `aws codebuild start-build`; everything that touches AWS runs on AWS compute, so no workflow holds a static AWS key and the only remaining GitHub dependency is the git clone, and the fleet is dispatched concurrently and polled together so a multi-service release costs the slowest service rather than the sum of all of them. It REQUIRES the aws CLI, CODEBUILD_PROJECT_PREFIX and AWS_REGION (exit 8 / exit 2 without them). "github" fires GitHub Actions workflows via `gh workflow run` and requires the gh CLI; it stays for a repo that deploys somewhere with no AWS account behind it. "custom" means the project DOES deploy, by a procedure /deploy does not dispatch — an SSH push to a box, a hosting provider's own CLI, a hand-run script; deploy.sh stops at exit 2 BEFORE any bump, commit or tag, and the project's own rule under rules/project/ carries the actual steps. "none" means the project does not deploy at all. Empty/missing → "codebuild", so an unprovisioned project fails loud with exit 2 before any bump rather than silently shipping through the other backend; any value outside the four fails the same way. custom and none are deliberately NOT a taxonomy of deploy mechanisms — splitting them by transport would put a description of a deploy in a config file instead of in the deploy script that runs it. Never sniffed from the repo: a release boundary must not guess where it is shipping from. RUNTIME-READ placeholder: consumed by deploy.sh via `jq -r '.DEPLOY_BACKEND // ""' .claude/sync-substitutions.json` at execution time, NOT substituted into any kit template at sync time. See handbook §6.5.
_placeholders_referenced_by_kit.CODEBUILD_PROJECT_PREFIX: Prefix that maps a DEPLOY_WORKFLOWS filename to a CodeBuild project name: deploy-<service>.yml → <prefix><service> (prefix 'myapp-deploy-' + deploy-worker.yml → project myapp-deploy-worker). This is why DEPLOY_WORKFLOWS stays the single service list under both dispatching backends — there is no second list to drift out of step with the first. REQUIRED when DEPLOY_BACKEND is "codebuild" (deploy.sh exits 2 without it); ignored under "github", "custom" and "none". RUNTIME-READ placeholder: consumed by deploy.sh via `jq -r '.CODEBUILD_PROJECT_PREFIX // ""' .claude/sync-substitutions.json` at execution time, NOT substituted into any kit template at sync time. See handbook §6.5.
_placeholders_referenced_by_kit.CODEBUILD_MIGRATE_PROJECT: CodeBuild project name for the migration phase, when it does not follow the CODEBUILD_PROJECT_PREFIX pattern applied to MIGRATE_WORKFLOW. Empty/missing → derived the same way every app project is (migrate.yml → <prefix>migrate). Only meaningful when DEPLOY_BACKEND is "codebuild" and MIGRATE_WORKFLOW is set; the migrate gate itself is identical on both dispatching backends (watched to completion, a real failure aborts with exit 19 before any app ships). RUNTIME-READ placeholder: consumed by deploy.sh via `jq -r '.CODEBUILD_MIGRATE_PROJECT // ""' .claude/sync-substitutions.json` at execution time, NOT substituted into any kit template at sync time. See handbook §6.5.
_placeholders_referenced_by_kit.AWS_ACCOUNT_ID: 12-digit AWS account ID this project's infra lives in. RUNTIME-READ placeholder: read by the AI via `jq -r '.AWS_ACCOUNT_ID // ""' .claude/sync-substitutions.json` when running AWS CLI (per rules/cli-utilities.md), NOT substituted into any kit template. Use to confirm `aws sts get-caller-identity` matches the intended account before any operation. Empty = project has no AWS.
_placeholders_referenced_by_kit.AWS_REGION: Default AWS region for this project's resources, e.g. us-east-1. RUNTIME-READ placeholder: read via `jq -r '.AWS_REGION // ""' .claude/sync-substitutions.json` and passed as an explicit `--region` on every AWS CLI command; never the shell default. Empty = project has no AWS.
_placeholders_referenced_by_kit.AWS_PROFILE: Named AWS CLI profile for this project's AWS account, e.g. nextage. Provisioned via `aws login --profile <name>` (browser console sign-in, login_session in ~/.aws/config) — one profile per ACCOUNT named for the account/org, shared by every project in that account; NEVER created manually from static keys, and never from app runtime keys in .env. See rules/cli-utilities.md "Profile provisioning". RUNTIME-READ placeholder: read via `jq -r '.AWS_PROFILE // ""' .claude/sync-substitutions.json` and passed as an explicit `--profile` on every AWS CLI command. Empty = project has no AWS.
_placeholders_referenced_by_kit.SHARED_MODULE_DIR: Directory of the workspace that holds the shared module and its test scaffolding, relative to the repo root — e.g. "apps/shared" in a monorepo, "src" or "." in a flat repo, "packages/core" elsewhere. Supplies the DESTINATION for the vitest scaffolding under _claude-project/templates/testing/, which has no fixed home: vitest.config.ts lands at <SHARED_MODULE_DIR>/vitest.config.ts and every other file at <SHARED_MODULE_DIR>/test/<name>. Those files sync in `template` mode — the PROJECT owns them, so an adaptation is never reverted; the kit still surfaces its improvements as `kit-only` (offered) when untouched or `template-drift` (informational) when adapted, and `--ack-file` records "seen it, keeping mine" so a declined drift stops re-reporting until the kit changes again. Empty/missing = the project has no shared test module, and the scaffolding is skipped entirely rather than landing somewhere wrong. See handbook §11.13.
_placeholders_referenced_by_kit.DB_ENGINE: Which database engine this project runs on, and the single gate deciding which engine-specific kit guidance applies. FIVE values, and the distinction between the first and the last is the point: "" (empty) = NOT YET DECLARED — the walkthrough re-surfaces it every sync, and engine-specific rules must NOT assume an engine; "PostgreSQL" = rules/postgres-drizzle.md and the postgres-neon-drizzle skill apply; "SQLServer" = rules/sqlserver-drizzle.md applies (Drizzle's MSSQL dialect, 1.0 RC channel); "Other" = the project HAS a database that is neither (SQLite, MySQL, DuckDB, something exotic) — every kit engine rule stands down and the project supplies its own under rules/project/; "None" = the project has NO database at all, so the engine rules, db-branch.mjs and the DB test scaffolding are all moot. Empty NEVER means "no database" — that is what "None" is for, and conflating them lets a project with an undeclared engine silently inherit Postgres advice. Add to _intentionally_empty ONLY if the project genuinely cannot answer yet; the honest answers for a no-DB project are "None", not empty. Values are matched EXACTLY and are case-sensitive. RUNTIME-READ placeholder: read by the AI via `jq -r '.DB_ENGINE // ""' .claude/sync-substitutions.json` at the top of any engine-specific rule or skill, NOT substituted into any kit template at sync time. See handbook §9.7 'Runtime-read placeholders'.

_documented_behavior: Three states per key. (1) Key MISSING from this file → /sync-dev-kit leaves {{KEY}} marker untouched in applied content; surfaces as a diff on every scan until populated. Use this for placeholders you haven't decided about yet. (2) Key present with EMPTY STRING value → /sync-dev-kit substitutes {{KEY}} with empty string; consumer file ends up with the real empty value (e.g. FOO=""). Use this as the explicit opt-out for features that support being disabled (e.g. GITFLOW_*). (3) Key present with NON-EMPTY value → normal substitution. Missing-vs-empty distinction is intentional: missing forces attention, empty signals informed disable.
_intentionally_empty_doc: Walkthrough metadata used by /sync-dev-kit Step 1.5. Keys listed here are skipped by the per-key walkthrough (the user has already decided to leave them off). Empty values NOT in this list get re-surfaced on every sync until populated or explicitly disabled. The substitution engine ignores _-prefixed keys, so this metadata never affects {{KEY}} replacement behavior.
